message.content: The common ancestor of lions (family Felidae) and zebras (family Equidae) is the last common ancestor of all modern mammals, which lived around 200–250 million years ago during the late Triassic period. This ancestor was a small, shrew‑like mammal that gave rise to the diverse lineages that eventually led to the distinct families of felids and equids.
